clue.text: Act provocatively, so altercation may be the outcome

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase so altercation are rearranged, and the result is what may come out of them

explanation.surface: Behaving provocatively, the clue warns, is likely to end in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be the outcome' signals an anagram of SO ALTERCATION. The definition is a fitting result, since trailing one's coat invites exactly that altercation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from dragging a coat for someone to tread on, deliberately inviting a fight.

clue.text: Don't be offended by trick pleasing some

parts.note: to take in is to deceive
good means pleasing or agreeable
part means some of something

explanation.surface: Advice not to be upset by a prank that some people enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something in a friendly spirit, without taking offence.

clue.text: Troubled with anxiety initially. I was first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word anxiety is taken

parts.note: led means was in front

explanation.surface: A worried person admits to having been the first to fret.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailed means caused pain or bother to, so afflicted.

clue.text: They depend on Hazel — and such as Larry

definitions.text: They depend on Hazel — and such as Larry

parts.words: They depend on Hazel — and such as Larry
parts.note: hazel catkins hang down and are named after the rear ends of young sheep, and Larry the Lamb was a character on BBC children's radio, so his rear end fits too

explanation.surface: Things that rely on someone called Hazel, and on a man called Larry.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel and Larry look like people; the hazel is a tree whose catkins hang (depend) from it, and Larry the Lamb was a famous British children's radio character.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangling catkins of hazel resemble the fluffy rear appendages of young sheep.

clue.text: Fruit with skin might be called bananas

parts.note: a nut is a fruit
a case is an outer covering

explanation.surface: A fruit in its peel might be called bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites thinking of real bananas; bananas is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person is slangily described as bananas.

clue.text: Confessor, having lost first daughter, became a factor

indicators.note: the first of the two Ds in the saint's name is the one that goes

parts.note: St Edward the Confessor was an English king and saint

explanation.surface: A priest hearing confessions becomes an agent after losing his eldest daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost first' removes the first D (daughter) of ST EDWARD. A factor is an estate manager.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland especially, an agent managing property on behalf of an owner.

clue.text: Waterproof suit, medium

definitions.meaning: the material an artist paints with

explanation.definitionFit: Oilskins are shortened to the plural, and oil paints are an artistic medium.

clue.text: Tedious at the start, becoming 'ectic in addition

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word Tedious is taken

parts.note: hotting up, with the h dropped as the apostrophe in 'ectic signals

explanation.surface: A dull start turns frantic later on.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ectic shows a dropped h, as in Cockney speech: becoming hectic is hotting up, here 'OTTING UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding up figures is summation.

clue.text: Nick — I come to a halt, he helps me get moving about

indicators.note: the letters are made to move around into a new order

parts.note: to stop is to come to a halt

explanation.surface: A man named Nick breaks down and someone helps get him going again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get moving about' rearranges I, STOP and HE HELPS ME. Nick is Old Nick, the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The demon of the Faust legend is a devil, and Old Nick is a name for the Devil.

clue.text: That's more like it — after training, I went the distance

indicators.note: training puts the words more like it through a regime that reshapes their letters
the clue's I has gone, so the letters of that word leave the rearranged pool

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner pleased with progress says that after a training session they managed the full course.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'after training' rearranges MORE LIKE IT, and 'I went' says that one I leaves the pool; the nine letters left make a unit of distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length equal to a thousand metres is a measure of distance.

clue.text: The capacity of drunken engineers

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A question about how much a group of tipsy engineers can hold.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of volume, a measure of capacity.

clue.text: Name of river and state of America

parts.note: Ind. is the abbreviation for Indiana, a US state
US stands for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A geography quiz asking for a river and a state of America.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the river's name; Indiana abbreviated as IND and US for America are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A major river of south Asia flowing through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Match is off

definitions.meaning: a fixture played on the opponents' ground

explanation.definitionFit: An away game is played at the other side's ground; someone who has left is not present.

clue.text: Ruin a beautiful woman

definitions.meaning: to spoil or wreck, as of hopes

explanation.definitionFit: To dish one's chances is to wreck them, and an attractive person is slangily called a dish.

clue.text: Past concealed by wicked beggar

indicators.note: something concealed by another is hidden inside it

parts.note: impish means mischievous or wicked
over means finished or past

explanation.surface: A past hidden by an evil vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beggar' is a verb, to reduce to poverty, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone destitute, as a verb.

clue.text: I am captivated by girl's face

indicators.note: being held captive by something means being enclosed within it

parts.note: Grace is a girl's name
contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: A speaker confesses to being smitten by a young woman's looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated by' is the container signal. 'face' looks like the girl's feature but is the definition, a noun for a pulled expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted expression of pain or disgust is a pulled face.

clue.text: "With men' is not exactly 'with it'

indicators.note: the words are not exactly as written, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment that saying 'with men' is not the same as saying 'with it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable, up to date and fully involved in what is going on.

clue.text: Compensation stops -— about time!

indicators.note: the barriers go round, so the word for time sits inside them

parts.note: dams stop or block water
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone whose payout has been halted exclaims that it is high time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'stops' looks like a verb but is a plural noun for barriers holding back water.
explanation.definitionFit: Money awarded by a court for loss or injury is a form of recompense.

clue.text: Flier coming in terror to land

indicators.note: the answer is coming in among the letters of the words terror to land

explanation.surface: A frightened air passenger in terror as the plane descends to land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an aircraft passenger; the flier is a small bird, eaten as a delicacy in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird, a bunting, is something that flies.

clue.text: Retribution is pursuing retreating Kentish men

indicators.note: following behind, so it comes after
going backwards, so the letters for Kentish men are read in reverse

parts.note: SE is south-east, the part of England where Kent lies
taken as written

explanation.surface: Justice chases men of Kent as they withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns both pieces backwards and 'is pursuing' puts the IS after them. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of vengeance gives her name to deserved punishment.

clue.text: House taking name from insect

indicators.note: taking N from the creature removes that letter

parts.note: the scorpion is loosely called an insect here, though it is an arachnid

explanation.surface: A family dynasty named after a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... from' removes N (name) from SCORPION. 'House' is an astrological house, a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A zodiac sign occupies one of the twelve divisions, or houses, of the astrological chart.

clue.text: Staying stormy and gloomy

indicators.note: a stormy state throws the letters of staying into turmoil

explanation.surface: Remaining in turbulent, dark weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the river Styx of the underworld, dark and dismal.

clue.text: Look for a match

explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look hard, and a peer is someone of equal standing.

clue.text: An award — in olden days, you came back without one

annotationWithheld.why: An award — in olden days, you came back without one (4): YE reversed gives the outer E...Y, but nothing in the clue as printed accounts for the MM, and no source found gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: An award — in olden days, you came back without one

clue.text: World shortage — there's no deuterium to be seen

indicators.note: saying the element is absent tells us to drop its symbol from the word

parts.note: a dearth is a scarcity
D is the chemical symbol for deuterium, heavy hydrogen

explanation.surface: A global scarcity: not a trace of heavy hydrogen to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no' removes D, the symbol for deuterium, from DEARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is the world we live on.

clue.text: There's nothing in a stratagem to provoke

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or stratagem
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A plot contains no intention to provoke.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or awaken anger or action.

clue.text: Thought I had every advantage initially

parts.note: I'd is a contraction of I had

indicators.note: the first letters of every and advantage are taken

explanation.surface: Someone believed they had every advantage at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or concept is something thought up.

clue.text: Took boat from sound anchorage

indicators.note: the clue asks for something sounding like the word for an anchorage

parts.note: roads, or a roadstead, is a sheltered anchorage offshore

explanation.surface: Someone takes a boat out from a safe harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: A road (usually roads or roadstead) is a stretch of water where ships can ride at anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: To row is to propel a boat with oars, so took a boat out under oar power.

clue.text: Sabbath is accompanied by religious observance and religious song

parts.note: pi is slang for pious
a ritual is a ceremonial observance

explanation.surface: The holy day comes with ceremony and hymn singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of devotional song from African American tradition.

clue.text: Help for the aged, moreover, carried by people with personal transport

indicators.note: a word carried by another is held inside it

parts.note: men are people
also means moreover
wheels is slang for one's own car

explanation.surface: Elderly people are helped by drivers who have their own cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' is the container signal; wheels is British slang for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A service delivering hot food to elderly people in their homes.
